# Chapter 16 · Tuskhold (SEALED — DM ONLY)

> **Act III, chapter 3 of 7.** Level **16** during, **17** on exit. 2 sessions. Highwater, YF 1105. Mirrowen: the plain of Tuskhold, its walls, its river-postern, and the Remembering Hall.
> Built on `campaign/02` Ch16 (and the Addendum's Ch16 routes), `campaign/00` §7 (Loss #2), `campaign/03` SEC-12, SEC-19, `campaign/04` (Mercy; Umbari's song is a requirement for Ending 2), `campaign/05` §5–§7 (footprints, discovery moments, Moss's upgrade #4), `truth/01` (NPC-021, NPC-008, NPC-022, NPC-004, NPC-005, NPC-057, NPC-003), `truth/03` (R-072, R-073, R-074, R-075, R-077, R-080, R-012, R-096), `truth/05` (EVT-31, EVT-32), `rules/02` (L16 targets; boss checklist). Shared rules in `_index.md` (read it first).
> **The point of this chapter:** Ash stands on a wall with people who were his enemies a month ago, and they hold. Then the wisest person in two worlds gives him everything she is, and he has to carry it.

## ★ Must-happen beats

### ★1 · The siege
The Hushed host (the deep-Hushed who wouldn't wake, the Heron's half of the Host if it split, and the Hushed dead of the Gate War) comes out of the greywilt on the plain at dawn. Tuskhold's walls, and the party in the middle. On their side: Brannoc's (or Fergan's) loyalists, the Free Clans, Russet Tamsworth, and the bear-folk who knelt to Gideon.
- **A. They march with the relief army.** From Cairn Answer, three days down off the Horngard with the Horned Host, the woken calves' families and Russet's Foxes. They arrive on the ridge above the plain the night before the assault (S16.3) and come in through the lines (SC 16-A link 1).
- **B. They get inside Tuskhold through a gate.** If the party went home first, or got separated, Ash opens Tuskhold's own minor Wellgate, the **Long Pool** in the Remembering Hall's undercroft, from the Ford Pool or Hollowmere. They surface inside the walls the night before (S16.3).
- **C. They're already in Tuskhold.** If they went straight there after Ch15 (or skipped the Horngard), they hold the walls with Nkemba until relief comes. Fight 27 is fought without the relief army; the relief arrives at Fight 28 phase 4 (the counter-charge is the relief coming over the ridge).
- **D. (If they're somewhere else entirely.)** Lark wakes in the night: "Gran Umbari is calling." She runs for the nearest still water. The party follows her or loses her. Either way, she crosses, and the beat is now "get to Lark." Use route B.

### ★2 · Umbari gives the song (Loss #2; EVT-31)
In the Remembering Hall at the siege's height, she gives the **full Sundering song**, memory to memory, to Ash, Clara and Lark. It costs her life. She asks them to honor it. Her last words seed the Tortoise (SEC-12 revealed).
- **A. In the Remembering Hall at the siege's height** (Fight 28 phase 3, SC 16-B). The Hall is being broken into; the party holds it while she sings.
- **B. On the walls, if the Hall falls** (SC 16-B fails, or the party is pinned on the wall): she has herself carried up the stair on a litter and sings from the parapet, over the battle. The Hushed below *stop* to listen.
- **C. Before the siege, at night**, if the party arrived early (route B, or the night before on route A): she won't wait. *"I'd rather give it while I can still hold it."* It happens in the Hall by lamplight, quietly, with only the party and Nkemba there. She dies at dawn, as the drums start. (This is the gentlest version. Let the player choose it by arriving early.)
- **D. If Ash refuses to let her** (asks her not to, physically stops her, leaves): `campaign/00` §7 rules. She does it anyway, in the night, with Lark, who carries it to Ash and Clara later through the bond. She leaves Ash a message carved on a long-stone (S16.8).

### ★3 · The siege breaks
A set-piece mass battle with a big turn: the woken calves' families, the Free Clans and the minotaurs fight side by side for the first time.
- **A. A counter-charge led by the party** (Fight 28 phase 4): out the main gate into the Warlord's line.
- **B. Gideon rallies the bear-folk and minotaurs on the walls** (his discovery: the aura covers the whole line) and they hold until the Hushed break.
- **C. Ash opens a gate behind the Hushed host** (the old drowned watering-pond on the plain is a minor Wellgate; Zeke can find it on Tuskhold's long-stone maps) and the Free Clans come through it from Hollowmere.

### ★4 · The clans unite (EVT-32)
At Umbari's funeral pyre (or her stone), the Free Clans, the Horned Host and Saffra swear one alliance behind "the hearers."
- **A. At Umbari's pyre** (S16.9, SC 16-C).
- **B. At the broken siege lines.** Brannoc (or Fergan) kneels to Ash first, in the mud, and the rest follow.
- **C. At the Great Telling in Saffra a week later**, if tensions run high (the Host and the Free Clans nearly come to blows at the pyre). Ash tells the story of the siege; the Tale-Keepers make it law.

## Scenes

### S16.1 · Down off the Horngard (opening; relationship beats)
Three days of marching with an army that was trying to kill them in the spring. Pick two:
- **Brannoc and Gideon** walk at the front together and don't talk for a whole day. On the second day Brannoc says, "Your bear knelt to you. Mine knelt to a bird." Gideon: "Then kneel to something better." (If Fergan leads instead, Fergan asks Gideon to teach him a Tall Folk oath. Gideon teaches him the one he swore at the Ford Stone.)
- **Ama** won't leave Lark. She asks, through Lark, why the sky moves. Lark teaches her a warren clapping game. By the third day minotaur soldiers are playing it at the cookfires.
- **Russet Tamsworth** (R-072) walks beside Ash for an hour and says nothing, then: "My father said Tall Folk took the song. He was right. You're giving it back. I don't know what to do with that." (If Ash is honest about the glimmer, Russet's edge moves toward EVT-32 early: he'll speak first at the pyre.)
- **Zeke** reads Tuskhold's siege-maps that Nkemba sent by owl. He finds the drowned watering-pond on the plain and says, "That's a Wellgate. A small one." (Sets up ★3 C.)
- **Bart** rides on a minotaur's horn for a full day and refuses to get off. Bart (to Ash): *"I've decided I'm Mirrowen now. I have a horn."*

### S16.2 · The antlers (Moss's upgrade #4; free story beat)
On the last night on the ridge, Moss goes off alone to the edge of the greywilt. Ash (or whoever follows) finds him with his hands in the grey grass, and the grass going green under his fingers in a slow ring. When he stands, the antler-shadow that's followed him since Bearback doesn't fade. The antlers are *there*: real, mossy, small white flowers in the tines. He touches them like a man touching a new scar. "Well," he says. "That's that, then. No more hats."
- **Mechanical:** **upgrade #4** (`campaign/05` §7). From now on, **once per encounter** Moss can take the Hart's true form for **one full round** (the stat block at the end of this file). This replaces the once-per-tier Hart round from Act II. Ch17's Aranhollow piece (or Ch19's) brings upgrade #5.
- **Story:** minotaur sentries see him and go silent. One old bull takes off his helmet. By morning the whole Host knows Old Mossback walks with them. (R-073: Russet, who thought the Stag was a story for kits, sees it and says nothing for the rest of the night. EVT-25 if it hasn't happened.)

### S16.3 · The night before (SC 16-A)
Inside Tuskhold. The city is hungry, orderly, brave. **Nkemba** (NPC-183, provisional) runs the walls. **Grandmother Umbari** (NPC-021) is in the Remembering Hall and can no longer stand. She asks for Ash. The night is SC 16-A: preparing the defense, link by link, with Umbari's request woven in.
- **What Umbari says** (whichever route): she tells them what she's going to do tomorrow. She doesn't ask permission. She asks them to be there. *"I have carried this song for ninety years. I have been remembering it for you. Tomorrow I'll give it to you, because tomorrow is when I'll have the strength left to give it whole. After that I won't need to carry anything."* (If Ash argues: R-074, she has no blind spot. She's kind and immovable. "You'll grieve. Good. It means it mattered.")
- **The player should understand that this is going to happen,** and that it's her choice. Don't hide it. The tension of the fight tomorrow is that they're protecting the room where she's dying.

### S16.4 · Dawn: the grey comes (★1; Fight 27)
The plain goes still at first light. No wind, then no birds, then the grass greys in a line a mile long. Out of it walk the deep-Hushed, the Heron's half of the Host (if it split), and behind them, rank on rank, the **Hushed dead of the Gate War** in four-hundred-year-old harness, carrying a war-mammoth's grey bulk in their middle. There are grey siege towers, built of still-water ice that doesn't melt. Fight 27 is the first assault on the walls.

### S16.5 · The Warlord (Fight 28 phases 1–2)
When the first assault breaks, the second doesn't wait. At its head walks **Dunmore Breakhorn**, the Hushed Warlord (NPC-190, provisional): the oldest of the Gate War dead, a minotaur marshal who died four hundred years ago holding the Horngard's gate *for* the Wardens, and was Hushed where he fell. The Heron woke him. He doesn't know which side he's on. He knows only that he's still holding a gate.
- **Zeke** (Insight or History DC 19, or automatic if he read the Wardens' stones in Ch15): his harness carries the Wardens' four-beast sigil. "He fought *for* them. He was on our side."
- **Moss** knows him by sight. "Dunmore. Oh, old friend."

### S16.6 · The Remembering Hall (★2 A; Fight 28 phase 3; SC 16-B)
The main gate falls. The Hushed pour into the lower city, and the Warlord turns, unerringly, toward the Hall, because the Stillness knows what's in it. Umbari begins to sing. The party holds the Hall's doors and its long-stone aisle while she does.
- **The song, as the party hears it:** not words, not yet. A memory poured into them, as if they're remembering something they never saw: a ford at dusk, four great beasts standing in the water, a young woman with a grey-flecked eye singing, and the world *coming apart along a seam* like a river splitting around a stone. Ash, Clara and Lark each feel it settle in them like a second heartbeat.
- **Zeke** doesn't receive the song, but he hears its *words* for the first time and starts writing them down without meaning to. (Seed for Ch17's discovery: he'll be able to speak them.)

### S16.7 · The counter-charge (★3; Fight 28 phase 4)
Umbari stops singing. The Hall goes quiet. Outside, the battle hasn't stopped. Somebody has to open the gate and go out. Brannoc (or Fergan) looks at Ash. *"Hearer. Do we go?"* The party leads the charge, or Gideon holds the walls, or Ash opens a gate behind the host. **Ama** slips away from her guards and is on the gate-stair when it opens, singing the warren clapping-song Lark taught her. The calves' families hear her. They charge.

### S16.8 · Umbari (EVT-31)
After the counter-charge, or at dawn (route C), or in the night (route D). She's lying on the longest stone. She's very small now. She asks for the party, Lark (and Clara), Nkemba and Brannoc.
- **To Lark:** "Little one. You carry two halves. Don't let anyone tell you that's too much."
- **To Clara** (or through Lark to Clara): "You were made to sing. Not for him. Not for anyone. For the song."
- **To Brannoc** (R-075, her last words name him): "Regent. You were a good father who made a terrible bargain. Be a good father now."
- **To Moss:** she says his true name. "Mossoran. Tell your sister I forgive her. She'll need to hear it from someone."
- **To Ash (SEC-12 revealed, the last words):** ***"The Old Tortoise sleeps where the sea has stopped. Three songs at the Glass, and the shell will listen. Even still water remembers the rain."*** And then she doesn't say anything else.
- **Route D's long-stone message** (if Ash refused): carved by her own trunk in the night on a fresh stone: *"Hearer: I asked you to honor it. You did. You tried to stop me. That's honor too. Three songs at the Glass, and the shell will listen. Even still water remembers the rain. — U."*
- **What this does:** every elephant-folk in Tuskhold touches their trunk to the stone she lies on. The Hushed outside the walls, the ones still standing, kneel in the grey grass. The song has gone into the people who'll need it.
- **Don't rush this.** Ask the player if Ash says anything. Then let Gideon go first if he doesn't.

### S16.9 · The pyre (★4; SC 16-C; EVT-32)
Elephant-folk don't burn their dead. They raise a long-stone over them and carve what they remembered. But Umbari asked for a pyre, "so the smoke goes over the walls, so everyone can see it." So there's a pyre, and a stone. At it, the Free Clans, the Horned Host, Saffra's Tale-Keepers and the bear-folk stand in the same field for the first time in four hundred years, and they nearly fight. SC 16-C is the chain that turns that field into an alliance.

### S16.10 · After (funeral games; exit)
Three days of funeral games. Tuskhold's **memory contests** and the **long-stone puzzle** (side-activity window). Brannoc gives Ash a thing from the Ironhorn armory (treasure). Nkemba becomes Rememberer and carves the first line of Umbari's stone; she asks Ash what it should say. Then they go home, because the Hall of Two Rivers is waiting and three people are now carrying the song that opens it.

## Skill challenges

> Chain format and DCs from `_index.md` §3. **L16 DCs:** easy 15, standard 17, hard 19, very hard 21. Reliable Talent makes Ash's expertise links safe; every chain has links he can't take.

### SC 16-A · "The Night Before" · L16 · 6 links, Pressure 0–3
**Situation:** one night to ready a hungry city for the assault. Every link the party wins is a **Siege Asset** for Fight 27 and Fight 28 (listed). Pressure means the dawn comes early.

| # | Link | Ways through | Success (Siege Asset) | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Through the lines (route A only; route B/C skip it) | Stealth DC 17 (group: half must pass) · Lark's song into the sentries' dreams (automatic; Lark can't add advantage to a waking check tomorrow) · Brannoc's Host drums a false signal (automatic if Brannoc turned) | In, unseen | In, but seen: Pressure +1 |
| 2 | The walls: who stands where | History or Insight DC 17 (reading Nkemba's maps) · Gideon's Persuasion DC 17 · Zeke's long-stone maps (Investigation DC 19) | **Asset: Line Placed.** Fight 27's Tide starts +1 | Units squabble over position: Pressure +1 |
| 3 | The grey towers: how do you fight ice that doesn't melt? | Arcana DC 19 (Zeke: "it's *still*, not cold; shake it") · Nature DC 17 (Moss: "thunder") · an experiment with a thunderwave on a shard (no roll; costs a 1st-level slot) | **Asset: Thunder Known.** Towers take double thunder damage, and the Wallguard's war-horns can do it too (the walls' horns deal 10 thunder per round to one tower) | Discovered mid-fight (round 2) instead |
| 4 | The undercroft: the Long Pool | Survival or Arcana DC 17 · Ash finds its key note (Performance DC 19, or automatic with the locket) | **Asset: Back Door.** The Long Pool can be opened in Fight 28 phase 3 to bring help into the Hall (Russet's Foxes come up through it: SC 16-B gets one automatic success) | The pool is known but not ready |
| 5 | Feed the wall | Sleight of Hand DC 17 (Ash "finds" the Host's supply wagons' hidden ale, salt pork and honey cakes) · Persuasion DC 17 (Brannoc's quartermaster) · Goodberry, Create Food and Water, Heroes' Feast (automatic) | **Asset: Fed.** The Wallguard's Exhaustion (raft lost) is cleared. Tide +1 in Fight 28 | Hungry: no change |
| 6 | Umbari asks for Ash (the last link; can't fail) | Sit with her. No roll. | **Asset: Remembered.** In Fight 28 phase 3, Ash has advantage on every check in SC 16-B | — |

**Pressure 1:** dawn comes an hour early; one link (the DM's choice of the unattempted) can't be attempted. **Pressure 2:** the Hushed attack in the dark; Fight 27 starts in **dim light** (the party's darkvision matters; the Wallguard has disadvantage on round 1 attacks). **Pressure 3:** a Hushed scout reaches the undercroft; link 4 fails automatically and Fight 28 phase 3 starts with a **Greywilt Choir** already in the Hall.

### SC 16-B · "Hold the Hall" (★2 A) · inside Fight 28 phase 3 · 6 successes before the phase ends
Run **inside** the fight. Each round of phase 3, each party member can spend their **action** on a link instead of attacking (or a bonus action, where noted). Umbari needs **6 successes** to finish the song before the phase's pool is gone or round 11 arrives, whichever is first. Each round in which no success is scored, the Warlord's line advances one aisle-stone toward her (four stones to the dais).

| Link | Who | Ways through | Success | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hold the doors** | anyone | Athletics DC 19 (bar the door against the Honor-Guard's push) · a wall of force, a forcecage across the door, a Moss Hart *Stand* (automatic) | 1 success | The Honor-Guard pushes one aisle-stone further |
| **Sing with her** | Ash, Clara, Lark (bonus action) | Performance DC 19 (Ash: advantage from Asset: Remembered) · the duet: Ash and Clara together, one roll, advantage, **counts double** (Twin Bond 3+) | 1 success (2 for the duet) | Umbari falters: the next success needs two (narrate her losing a line and finding it) |
| **Keep her breathing** | Moss, Gideon, anyone with healing | Medicine DC 19 · Lay on Hands (any amount: automatic) · a healing spell of 5th level or higher (automatic) | 1 success | No effect, but her breath rattles |
| **Lay the dead to rest** | anyone | Religion DC 19 (the Gate War's rest-words, which Umbari half-sings between verses) · Lark's song (automatic, once) | 1 success, and one Hushed Honor-Guard in the Hall drops (laid to rest) | That Honor-Guard attacks the speaker (one attack, advantage) |
| **Read the words** | Zeke | History or Arcana DC 19 (writing down the words as she sings them) | 1 success, and Zeke keeps the words (Ch17: his discovery is automatic) | He keeps half the words (Ch17: History DC 19 to finish them) |
| **The back door** | anyone at the Long Pool | (Asset: Back Door) Ash opens it, Performance DC 19 or automatic with the locket | 1 success, and Russet's Foxes come up through the pool (+2 Foxes, use Wallguard numbers) | — |

**6 successes:** the song is given whole (**EVT-31**, ★2 A). Umbari stops singing. The Hall is very quiet. Phase 3 ends at once and phase 4 begins (the counter-charge).
**If phase 3's pool runs out first** (the party killed the Warlord's third form before the song was done): the Warlord falls back, but the song isn't done. Umbari finishes it in the quiet after the battle, slower, and dies at dusk (★2 C's gentler version, delayed). Nothing is lost except time.
**If the Warlord's line reaches the dais** (four aisle-stones advanced): she can't be reached by the party for the rest of phase 3. She has herself carried to the parapet (**★2 B**). The song finishes from the wall, and the Hushed outside stop to listen (phase 4: every Hushed creature outside loses its first turn).

### SC 16-C · "One People" (★4; EVT-32) · at the pyre · 5 successes before 3 failures
**Situation:** at Umbari's pyre, the Host, the Free Clans, Saffra and the bear-folk stand in one field. They don't trust each other. Old grievances are close. One wrong word and it's a brawl. Ash (and anyone) speaks.

| Link | The problem | Ways through | Lever (automatic) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The Host and the hare-folk.** The Host occupied Hollowmere. Mother Burdock's people burned. | Persuasion DC 19 · Insight DC 17 (find the bull who sheltered a warren-family; there was one) | Brannoc kneels to Burdock first (if he turned and Ash asks him to) |
| 2 | **The foxes.** Russet won't swear to "horns" | Persuasion DC 19 · Deception doesn't work on Russet (he'll walk) | Ash was honest with Russet about the glimmer (S16.1): he speaks first |
| 3 | **Saffra's neutrality.** The Tale-Keepers trade with everyone | Performance DC 19 (a story at the pyre) · Persuasion DC 19 (Saffi) | Ash won the Great Telling in Ch14 (Saffi: "I don't need convincing. I need a better story than the one about the bird.") |
| 4 | **The bear-folk.** They kneel only to the Hearth-Warden | Gideon's Persuasion DC 17 (his oath, spoken in front of the pyre) · Religion DC 17 | Gideon led the line in Fight 27 or 28 (his discovery) |
| 5 | **The dead.** Two hundred of Tuskhold's own died. Who pays? | Persuasion DC 21 · Ash offers something real (the calf-price silver from Ch15; his own weapon on the pyre; a promise he'll keep: no roll, if the player means it) | Brannoc pays the calf-price to every family, by herd-law, before he's asked |
| 6 | **Who leads?** Everyone looks at Ash. | Persuasion DC 19 (Ash says "not me": the alliance swears to "the hearers" instead) · Intimidation doesn't work here | Ama walks up and takes Ash's hand. (Automatic, if Ama was woken. Narrate it and let the player decide what Ash does.) |

**5 successes:** **EVT-32.** One alliance behind "the hearers." Ronan Ironvoice drums it, Saffi tells it, Nkemba carves it. **FAC moves:** FAC-07 (Horned Host) and FAC-08 (Free Clans) → **Allied, united.**
**3 failures:** the field nearly breaks. Use **★4 route C**: a week later, at the Great Telling in Saffra, Ash tells the story of the siege (Performance DC 17; three tries; Saffi will let him go first). EVT-32 lands there. The cost is a week (Ch17 starts later: the Hall's turn of light is a week nearer Midsummer; nothing else).

### FIGHT 27 · The Walls · Ch16 · Significant (objective mass combat) · Party level 16

**Target numbers (L16):** total HP **630** · enemy DPR **92** (12% of effective HP 764) · AC 17–18 · attack +9 to +11 · DC 16–17.
**HP math (shown):** Hushed War-Mammoth 230 · 2 Grey Siege Towers × 80 = 160 · 4 Hushed Gate-War Shieldbearers × 60 = 240 → **630**. Party output 140 × 5.5 rounds ≈ 770 × ~80% (objectives, movement, the towers' height) ≈ 616. **Expected 5–6 rounds.**
**DPR math (vs party AC ~18–21):** War-Mammoth (2 × Gore 25 × 0.55 = 27.5; Trample recharge ~ +8 averaged) ≈ **35** · Shieldbearers 4 × (2 × 14 × 0.55) ≈ **31** (only 2–3 engage the party at a time: ~**23**) · Towers 2 × archers (12 × 0.55 × 2) ≈ **26** → **~84–92**.

**Battlefield: Tuskhold's west wall** (crop-friendly: the wall as a long horizontal strip, 40 ft high, 20 ft wide walk; the plain below; two gate-towers; the stair down into the city behind).
1. **The wall-walk.** 20 ft wide, crenellated (half cover). Elephant-folk need it wide; Tall Folk have room to move.
2. **The grey towers.** Two siege towers of still-water ice (*Grey Siege Tower*, below) rolling toward the wall at 10 ft per round. When one reaches the wall (round 3 if unhindered), its bridge drops and Shieldbearers come across.
3. **The war-horns.** Four great bronze horns on the wall, one every 60 ft. (With Asset: Thunder Known, a horn blown as an action deals 10 thunder damage to one tower within 120 ft. Anyone can blow it; Athletics DC 15, or automatic for a Large creature.)
4. **The mammoth's breach.** Below the north gate-tower, the Hushed War-Mammoth is ramming the wall. Each round it hits the wall (no roll), the wall's **breach track** advances 1 (0–4). At 4, a 20-ft section of wall-walk collapses (DC 18 Dex save or fall 40 ft, 4d6 and prone, into the plain among the Hushed).
5. **The plain.** Grey grass, still water in the ditches (still-water rules: DC 17 Wis or 3d8 psychic and speed 0 until the end of turn; Gideon's aura protects).

**Units on the field (narrative; no stat blocks needed).** Track a **Battle Tide** from −3 (the west wall falls) to +3 (the assault breaks). Start at 0 (+1 Line Placed, +1 Shieldbulls came back, −1 raft lost).
- *Allied units:* **Tuskhold Wallguard** (Nkemba), **the Bear-Den** (Hulda Greypaw), **the Horned Host's line** (Brannoc or Fergan) in the gate-towers, **Russet's Foxes** (archers), **the calves' mothers** (Breeda Stonefield, if the Host split).
- *Enemy units:* **the deep-Hushed host** (beastfolk who wouldn't wake: grey eyes, no voice), **the Gate War column** (Hushed dead in old harness), **the Heron's half of the Host** (if split).
- At the end of each round: **+1** Tide if the party met the phase's objective that round (or saved a unit from a named threat); **−1** if a tower reached the wall, the breach track advanced past 2, or an allied unit broke.
- **Gideon leads an army (discovery moment; once per day from now on):** as an action, Gideon lets Ursk's mark show fully. His **aura extends along the whole wall-walk** (every allied creature on the wall, out to 300 ft, gains its benefits) until the end of his next turn, and the Bear-Den and the Host's line both roar. Tide +1. (This is the moment the bear-folk and the minotaurs fight as one line for the first time.)

**Opening.** Dawn. The towers are 60 ft from the wall. The mammoth is at the north gate-tower's foot. The Shieldbearers are on the towers. The party is on the wall-walk wherever SC 16-A placed them.
**Enemy plan.** The Hushed don't think, but the Heron does, and she planned this: **towers to the wall, mammoth through it.** The Shieldbearers fight whoever is on the bridge. The towers' grey archers shoot whoever is blowing a horn. The mammoth ignores everything except the wall, until someone hurts it, and then it goes for them.

**PHASE 1 · rounds 1–2 · "Stop the towers"**
- Both towers roll. Each takes damage from the party, from the war-horns (with Thunder Known) and from Moss's earth-shaping. Bring one down before it reaches the wall and Tide +1.
- **Counter (Zeke's area spells):** *Telegraph (round 1):* the Shieldbearers on the tower-tops step apart from each other, 20 ft between each. A Fireball on one tower-top catches one of them, not four. (Fire doesn't hurt still-water ice at all; thunder does double.)

**PHASE 2 · trigger: a tower reaches the wall, both towers fall, or round 3 · "The bridge and the breach"**
- *Telegraph (round 2):* the mammoth backs up twenty paces. The ground shakes. Then it comes.
- **OBJECTIVE + TERRAIN change:** the breach track starts moving (feature 4). Any tower still standing drops its bridge, and Shieldbearers cross. The party must split: hold the bridge, or stop the mammoth. (They can't do both well. That's the point.)
- If Gideon uses *leads an army* here, the wall holds no matter what the breach track says until his next turn ends.

**PHASE 3 · trigger: the mammoth falls, the breach track hits 4, or round 5 · "The ditch"**
- *Telegraph (round 4):* the ditch-water at the wall's foot stops moving. The grey climbs the wall like frost.
- **TERRAIN change:** greywilt climbs the wall. Every space on the wall-walk within 10 ft of the outer parapet becomes still-water terrain (rules as feature 5). If the wall breached, the party fights in the rubble-gap with the Hushed coming in through it.
- **Objective:** clear the wall of everything grey. When the last Shieldbearer and the mammoth are down, the first assault breaks.

**FINAL BEAT.** The first assault breaks: the Hushed walk backward into the greywilt, slowly, all at once. Silence. Then, from the grey a mile out, a single war-horn that hasn't been blown in four hundred years. (Fight 28 begins after a short rest's worth of time: the party gets one short rest.)
**Fail-forward.** The west wall falls (Tide −3): the party falls back into the city's first street. Fight 28 phase 1 is fought in the street instead of at the breach, and phase 2 (the gate collapse) is skipped: the Hushed are already in. (One fewer phase, but the Hall is closer to the fighting: SC 16-B needs 7 successes.)
**Rewards.** Tide carried into Fight 28 (each point of Tide above 0 is one fewer Honor-Guard in phase 1). The mammoth's grey tusks (story; Nkemba carves them into Umbari's stone later).
**DM notes.** ~84–92 per round against 764 effective → 6 rounds ≈ 70% before healing. If the party is cruising, the second tower brings a second Shieldbearer pair. If struggling, the Host's line takes the bridge (one fewer Shieldbearer). Pacing guard: past round 6, the mammoth charges through the breach no matter what the track says, and the fight ends when it falls.

### FIGHT 28 · The Hushed Warlord · Ch16 · **BOSS** · Party level 16

**Target numbers (L16):** boss HP (all phases) **980** (cap **1,260** with three form or objective changes) · boss + adds DPR **76 sustained / 115 spike** · AC 17–18 · attack +9 to +11 · DC 16–17 · boss best saves **+7 to +9**.
**HP math (shown):**
- **Dunmore's pools:** Phase 1 **240** · Phase 2 **230** · Phase 3 **200** · Phase 4 **210** = **880**.
- **Adds ≈ 2 × DPR (280):** Phase 1: 3 Honor-Guard × 60 = 180 (minus 1 per point of Tide above 0 from Fight 27) · Phase 3: 1 Greywilt Choir 100 → **~280**.
- **Total ≈ 1,160** (under the 1,260 cap; three changes of different type). Party output 140 × 12 ≈ 1,680 × ~70% (Legendary Resistance, the gate collapse, phase 3's split attention between SC 16-B and the fight, phase 4's movement) ≈ 1,176. **Expected ~12 rounds.**
- **Nova check:** pools don't carry over. A nova ends a phase; it never skips the song.
**DPR math (vs party AC ~18–21):**
- Dunmore: 3 Answer-of-Iron attacks × 20 (2d12 + 7 = 20) × 0.55 = **33**.
- Legendary actions: ~1.5 uses per round × ~11 = **16**.
- Adds: P1 3 Honor-Guard × (2 × 13 × 0.55) = **43** (fades fast); P3 the Choir ≈ **12**.
- Lair-style Siege Actions (initiative 20): ~**8**.
- **Sustained ≈ 70–78.** **Spike:** *Hold the Gate* (P2 opening: DC 17 Str, 44 bludgeoning to everyone in the gateway ≈ 44 × 3 × 0.6 ≈ 79) + a full Multiattack ≈ **112–115**.

**Battlefield: Tuskhold's main gate and the lower city, then the Remembering Hall** (two crop-friendly maps: **Map A**, the gate square: a 100-ft paved square inside the main gate, the gate itself 30 ft wide under a gatehouse, three streets leading up into the city, the Hall's long stair on the north side; **Map B**, the Remembering Hall: a 120-ft-long stone hall, 40 ft wide, two rows of standing long-stones forming an aisle, Umbari's dais at the far end, great doors at the near end, the undercroft stair and the Long Pool below).
1. **The gate (Map A).** Iron-bound timber, already cracking. Above it, the gatehouse (30 ft up, murder-holes).
2. **The three streets.** Barricades of carts and long-stones. Each holds a Tuskhold unit.
3. **The long stair.** 60 ft of broad steps from the gate square to the Hall's doors. The Warlord's path.
4. **The aisle-stones (Map B).** Twelve carved long-stones, each 15 ft tall, 5 ft wide: full cover. SC 16-B tracks the Warlord's line by aisle-stone (four to the dais).
5. **The Long Pool (undercroft).** A minor Wellgate. With Asset: Back Door, it can bring the Foxes in.

**Opening.** The second assault comes straight up the road to the main gate behind a single figure walking in front. The party is on the gatehouse or in the gate square (wherever Fight 27 ended). Umbari has been carried into the Hall. Nkemba is on the gatehouse. Brannoc (or Fergan) holds the left street; the Bear-Den holds the right; Russet's Foxes are on the roofs.
**Enemy plan.** **The Hall.** The Stillness knows what's in it. Dunmore goes for the gate, then the stair, then the Hall's doors, then the dais. He fights whatever stands in his way. **He doesn't target Ash first. He targets whoever is *holding a gate*,** because that's what he died doing and it's all he remembers: whoever is barring the doors, whoever stands in a gateway, whoever is on the stair between him and the Hall. (Gideon is the natural target. Make it obvious.)

**PHASE 1 · rounds 1–3 · "The breach" (Map A)**
- Dunmore and three Honor-Guard (fewer by Tide) break the outer gate and fight in the gateway. The gatehouse murder-holes are the party's (pour oil, drop stones: Siege Action below).
- He fights *for the gate*: he won't leave the gateway, and anyone in it with him is "holding" it.
- **Counter (Gideon's Protection):** *Telegraph (round 1):* Dunmore lifts his maul and points it, not at Ash, at Gideon. In old Mirrowen-tongue (Lark or Moss translates): "Gate-keeper. Stand aside or stand with me." From now on, Dunmore's *Answer of Iron* ignores Gideon's Protection reaction (he swings *through* the shield-arm: the reaction can't impose disadvantage on Dunmore's attacks). Gideon's aura still works.

**PHASE 2 · trigger: phase 1 pool reaches 0, or round 4 · "The gate falls" (TERRAIN)**
- *Telegraph (round 3):* the gatehouse groans. Dust comes down from the murder-holes. Nkemba shouts, "Off the gate! *Off!*"
- **Hold the Gate (phase 2 opening, automatic):** Dunmore plants his maul and *heaves*. The gatehouse comes down. Every creature in the gateway or on the gatehouse makes a **DC 17 Strength save** (Dex if they'd rather dive): *Failure:* 44 (8d10) bludgeoning and buried (Restrained; Athletics DC 17 action to dig out, by themselves or an ally). *Success:* half and pushed 15 ft out of the rubble.
- The gate square becomes **rubble** (difficult terrain everywhere except the three streets and the stair). The Hushed column pours in behind him: the three streets' units are engaged (no help this phase).
- Dunmore makes for the stair. He has to be stopped on it, or he reaches the Hall's doors at the end of round 7 regardless.
- **Counter (Moss's front-line beast):** *Telegraph:* his first swing in phase 2 is a sweep at knee height. *Answer of Iron* in phase 2 has the *Hamstring* rider (below): a Large or larger creature it hits has its speed halved until the end of its next turn. Moss's biggest forms get pinned on the rubble.

**PHASE 3 · trigger: phase 2 pool reaches 0, he reaches the Hall's doors, or round 7 · "The Remembering Hall" (OBJECTIVE; Map B)**
- *Telegraph (round 6):* from the Hall above, a sound: Umbari has started to sing. Every Hushed creature in the square turns its head toward it at once, like flowers to the sun. Dunmore stops. Then he climbs.
- **OBJECTIVE change: protect Umbari while she sings.** **SC 16-B runs inside this phase.** Dunmore's line (he and whatever Honor-Guard survive, plus a **Greywilt Choir** that seeps up through the floor-cracks) advances up the aisle.
- Dunmore's third form: he's *slower* (speed 20) and *harder* (the Hall's still air: *Unmoving*, below). He isn't trying to kill. He's trying to reach the dais and put his hand over her mouth.
- **The song stirs him.** Each success in SC 16-B also *stirs* Dunmore (he loses his reaction and his next legendary action). He hears it. He remembers something.

**PHASE 4 · trigger: SC 16-B reaches 6 successes, phase 3's pool reaches 0, or round 10 · "The counter-charge" (FORM + OBJECTIVE; back to Map A)**
- *Telegraph:* the song stops. In the quiet, Dunmore says, in old Mirrowen-tongue, "...Mossoran?" (If Moss is there.) Then the Stillness's grip *tightens*: he roars, and the grey comes up out of him like smoke, and he turns and goes down the stair at a run, back toward the gate, to *hold it against them*.
- **FORM change:** **Dunmore, the Last Gate.** He takes his stand in the ruined gateway, where he died four hundred years ago. He's his old self, fighting the wrong side: faster, every attack a sweep, and he holds the gate for the Hushed host outside (it can't be shut while he stands).
- **OBJECTIVE:** break him and charge through. **★3 lands here:** whichever route the player chooses. The party leads the charge out (A), Gideon holds the walls (B), or Ash opens the watering-pond gate behind the host (C: Performance DC 19 from the gatehouse wall, or the locket).
- **Ama's song (S16.7):** on round 1 of phase 4, she's on the gate-stair, clapping, singing Lark's warren song. The calves' families hear it and charge. Battle Tide +2. Every Hushed creature outside is **stirred** for one round.
- **Lark's discovery (once, phase 4):** as the Hushed dead fall, Lark sings them to rest. As a **bonus action**, she can lay to rest every Hushed dead creature within 60 ft that's below half its HP (no save). The square goes quiet in a spreading ring. She doesn't stop crying while she does it.

**FINAL BEAT.** Dunmore falls in the gateway, on his back, looking up. If Moss is there, he kneels by him. Dunmore says: "Did we hold it?" Moss says, "Yes. You held it." **He's laid to rest.** Outside, the Hushed host breaks: the ones who are only deep-Hushed sit down in the grey grass, waiting to be woken (they will be, over the next month: Ash, Clara, Lark, in a long patient walk across the plain).
**Fail-forward.** If the party is losing in phase 4: the relief army comes over the ridge (route C), or the Bear-Den comes down off the walls in a wall of fur and iron (Hulda Greypaw: "Hearth-Warden! *Down!*"), and the fight ends when Dunmore is surrounded. He stops, looks at the bear-folk, and says, "Ursk's people." He lowers his maul. He's laid to rest without a blow.
**Rewards.** **EVT-31** (if SC 16-B finished), ★3; Dunmore's maul, *Answer of Iron* (story; Brannoc asks to carry it at the pyre, because his own maul is also named Answer, and he never knew why); the Warlord's harness with the Wardens' sigil (Zeke wants it: SEC-08 is now proven in a museum-quality way).
**DM notes.** Expected **~12 rounds**: 3 + 3 + ~3 + ~3. Pacing guard: past round 10, if the last change was 4+ rounds ago, start phase 4 at once. If SC 16-B is going badly, Nkemba comes up the stair and spends her action on *Hold the doors* each round (auto-success, once, then she's downed: she survives). The Hall should feel like it might fall. It shouldn't fall unless the player stops trying.

- ***From the Murder-Holes (the party's).*** Phase 1 only, and only if a party member or Nkemba is on the gatehouse: oil and stones fall on the gateway: every enemy in it takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning or fire (the party's choice). This is the party's lair action, not his. Use it.

**Phases:** P1 the breach (gateway); ignores Protection. P2 the gate falls; *Hold the Gate*; Hamstring. P3 the Hall; *Unmoving*; speed 20; 4th Legendary Resistance; *The Old Oath*. P4 the Last Gate; speed 50; *Gore*; Sweep.
**Tactics:** he goes for whoever is holding a gate, door or stair. He fights in the gateway in phase 1 and won't be lured out. He never attacks Umbari himself (he only wants to stop the song; his hand over her mouth, not a blow). He never attacks a bear-folk who kneels (Ursk's people). If Moss speaks to him in old Mirrowen-tongue, he stops for one heartbeat (lose his next legendary action), once per phase.

#### HUSHED HONOR-GUARD
*Medium Undead (minotaur), Lawful Neutral · **Hushed dead***
**AC** 18 · **Initiative** −1 (9) · **HP** 60 (8d8 + 24)
**Speed** 30 ft.
Use the **Hushed Gate-War Shieldbearer** block above, with these changes:
- ***Interpose.*** When an attack hits Dunmore and this Honor-Guard is within 5 ft of him, it takes the hit instead.
- ***Halberd*** instead of Axe: reach 10 ft, *Hit:* 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
- **No** Shield-Wall.
*Tuned for party level 16: guard (priority-target counter)*

#### GREYWILT CHOIR (hazard-creature)
*Large swarm of grey silence, Unaligned*
**AC** 12 · **Initiative** +0 (10) · **HP** 100 · **Speed** 20 ft. (through stone cracks)
**Immunities** psychic, poison · **Vulnerabilities** thunder (double), radiant · **Condition Immunities** everything except Restrained (a forcecage holds it)
- ***What it is.*** The grey that seeps up through the Hall's floor, wearing the shapes of people who died quietly. It hums nothing, very loudly.
- ***Silence Aura.*** Every creature within 15 ft of it can't speak, sing or cast verbal spells. *SC 16-B's "Sing with her" link can't be attempted within 15 ft of it.*
- ***Grey Touch.*** *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 17, each creature in its space or within 5 ft at the start of its turn. *Failure:* 18 (4d8) psychic damage and speed 0 until the end of its next turn. *Success:* half damage only.
- ***Song Breaks It.*** Any success on *Sing with her* within 60 ft (outside its aura) deals 20 thunder damage to it.
*Tuned for party level 16: controller (anti-singer counter)*

### THE HART (Moss's true form; upgrade #4; ally stat block)

> **When:** from S16.2 on, **once per encounter**, Moss can take this form **for one full round** (from the start of his turn until the start of his next turn). It's a bonus action to change, and he can still act in the same turn. At upgrade #5 (Ch17 or Ch19), he can hold it for a whole phase of the finale. Moss's druid HP stays separate: damage to the Hart comes off the Hart's HP first, and anything left over carries to Moss when he changes back (like Wild Shape's temporary HP).
> *Tuned for party level 16–20: a story form. It's strong for one round and can't be repeated in the same fight. It isn't a second front-liner.*

#### MOSSORAN, THE MOSS-CROWNED HART
*Huge Celestial (Firstbeast), Neutral Good*
**AC** 19 (natural armor) · **HP** 150 (temporary; refreshes each encounter) · **Speed** 80 ft.

|   | Score | Mod | Save |   | Score | Mod | Save |   | Score | Mod | Save |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STR | 24 | +7 | +12 | DEX | 18 | +4 | +9 | CON | 22 | +6 | +11 |
| INT | 16 | +3 | +8 | WIS | (Moss's) | | (Moss's) | CHA | 20 | +5 | +10 |

**Resistances** necrotic, psychic, bludgeoning, piercing, slashing · **Condition Immunities** Charmed, Frightened, Stilled (the Mirror) · **Senses** truesight 60 ft. · **Languages** every language of beasts and growing things
**Traits**
- ***Old Mossback.*** Every Hushed creature (not Hushed dead) within 60 ft that can see him has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but him. Beastfolk allies within 60 ft have advantage on saves against being Frightened or Stilled.
- ***Warden of the Ford.*** Greywilt and still-water terrain within 30 ft of him ends while he's in this form.

**Actions** *(he takes one, plus his bonus action to change)*
- ***Antlers.*** *Melee Attack Roll:* +13, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 40 (6d10 + 7) piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) radiant damage. He makes two of these.
- ***Break the Line.*** He charges up to 80 ft in a straight line through enemies. *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 20, each creature in the line. *Failure:* 44 (8d10) bludgeoning damage and prone. *Success:* half damage and pushed aside.
- ***Carry.*** Up to six willing allies within 10 ft climb on or hold on. He moves up to 160 ft; none of them provoke opportunity attacks.
- ***Stand.*** Until his next turn, every enemy within 60 ft that can see him has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but him, and he gains 100 more temporary HP.
- ***Bloom.*** Moss and white flowers spread 30 ft around him: allies there regain 8d10 HP, every Hushed creature there makes a DC 19 Wis save or is stirred (recent Hushed are **woken** instead), and greywilt there ends for good.

**Rules notes:** The Hart round at upgrade #4 doesn't cost a spell slot or a Wild Shape use. Free scripted beats (Ch13's roots, Ch15's stand against his sister) don't use it either. In Ch18's fight with Vessimer, the Hart can't attack her (R-012). He can stand, carry, bloom and break the line around her.

## If the party goes off-route
- **They try to stop Umbari by force** (put her to sleep, carry her off). She's ninety, and she's the Rememberer of Tuskhold, and half the city is elephant-folk. They let the party do it, gently. She wakes at night (`campaign/00` §7) and does it anyway, with Lark (★2 D). Don't make it a fight. Make it a message on a stone.
- **They try to heal her** (Heal, Wish, a Potion of Supreme Healing). It works on her body for a day. She's not dying of a wound. She's spending herself, by choice, on purpose. Healing her just means she has the strength to give it whole (★2 C). If Zeke uses *Wish* to try to save her: the Wish asks him (in Umbari's voice) whether he wants to take her choice away. If he says yes, the Wish fails and Zeke can never cast it again (2024 *Wish* stress rule, flavored). If he says no, the Wish comforts her instead and she dies smiling.
- **They try to wake Dunmore** instead of laying him to rest. He's Hushed dead; he can't be woken. But a waking check *stirs* him, and if Moss speaks to him while he's stirred, he answers. Play the conversation. He still has to be laid to rest at the end. Moss does it, if anyone asks.
- **They skip the counter-charge and stay with Umbari.** Fine. ★3 B: Gideon (if he's on the wall) or Brannoc holds the walls, and the Hushed break when Ama sings. The party sits with her. Nothing is lost.
- **Brannoc wasn't turned, and the Host isn't with them** (Ch15's worst case: the Host split, or the party never went to the Horngard). The Heron's half of the Host is in the assault. Fight 27 gets 2 extra Shieldbulls (`ch14.md` block). **Fergan** brings what loyal bulls he can over the ridge as the relief (★3 C timing). At the pyre, SC 16-C link 5 is a hard DC 21 (no lever). Brannoc, if he's alive and unturned, sends a message: "I heard the old one died. Tell me what she said about me." Ash can go to him (Ch17's side chapter: a one-scene turn, SC 14-C with every lever automatic).
- **Clara isn't with them.** Umbari gives Clara's share to Lark (★2). Lark carries it through the bond. Ch17's Hall needs Clara to have received it: Lark gives it to her in S17.1, a scene with no roll, and the twins are now even. Don't penalize the player for this.
- **The party loses the siege** (Fight 28 fail-forward fails too). Tuskhold doesn't fall. Elephant-folk walls don't fall. The Hushed host breaks on the walls over three more days, and the party is carried out of the gateway rubble by Nkemba's Wallguard. The song is given from the parapet (★2 B), and Umbari dies on the wall at dusk with the party alive beside her. EVT-31 and EVT-32 still land. The cost: no Siege Asset gold, and Brannoc's gift waits until Ch17.
